docs.purpose: The mobile LIST binding (props half): LotMapBinding.tsx maps a situation of the choose-your-lot page (S-071, LIST with render.projection map) to a props tree (refs only); the shared renderer SurfaceRenderer.tsx (owned by shared_mobile_surface_binding) draws it, react-native-maps' MapView, Polygon and Marker included. It holds no display text of its own.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing itself: the mount passes the situation built by mobile/src/lib/lotMap.ts from the lookup response.
docs.under_126: **PROMOTED BINDING ENTRY** (MF-53; the MF-48 D-2 a form): a platform_shared census entry that owns the mobile LIST binding module, so R-13 totality holds while the map page owns no component.

identity.owner: Admin domain (Spec 126 §14 Target Files) — the conversion programme owns the row; no individual owner is named by Specs 126/127/128.
spec_refs: docs/specs/02-web-admin/126_maxbld_surface_standard.md §11b.2 dated note 2026-11-11 — the mobile LIST binding (MF-53)

versioning.why: A binding module has no wire contract of its own: its input is a situation whose shape is pinned by the consuming surface's goldens (mobile_parcel_disambiguation_map) and its output is a props tree. A change shows up as a golden or render-smoke failure of the consumer.
evidence: mobile/__tests__/lotMapPage.behaviour.test.tsx — the mobile LIST render smoke (FE-33 mobile case)

inputs.why: The situation arrives as an argument from the mount file.

outputs.why: A binding writes nothing; a form submit is handed back to the mount file.

state.why: No store: the library component holds its own local UI state.

staleness.why: It renders what it is given.

session.why: Its only consumer today is the MaxBLD search page; each consumer declares its own guard.

rls_class.why: It renders lookup data the consumer already read through GET /api/parcels/lookup (parcels and address points, Class B); it reads no table itself.
evidence: src/app/api/parcels/lookup/route.ts — the route the consumer calls

list.item_archetype: none — a binding renders the consumer's items (the map page: lot cards and map polygons)
list.recycling: none — the consumer's list is bounded (at most 10 lots)

checks.why: The module is listed in bindings.json modules and owned by this entry (FE-31 C-3); a module nobody owns is a hand-built component.

errors.why: Errors belong to the consuming surface; the binding throws on a missing content key or an unknown widget so a gap is loud.

metering.why: Rendering is not a metered product action.

config.why: No tunable of its own. The SEARCH profile requires debounce_ms and min_query_len, which have no "none" value: 0 states that the binding itself neither debounces nor gates on length. The consuming surface declares its own (mobile_parcel_search: 400 ms, 3 characters), and the screen applies them.
evidence: mobile/src/components/surfaces/LotMapBinding.tsx — SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS and SEARCH_MIN_QUERY_LEN re-exported from the consumer slice

sharing.why: Every converted mobile surface (the parcel search page first).
sharing.varies_by_surface: Only the props tree, content and data passed in.

notes: MF-53 (plan v4 §3, §8 item 2; the MF-48 D-2 a form for a second archetype): archetype LIST; the render half stays SurfaceRenderer.tsx (shared_mobile_surface_binding), which lists SEARCH and LIST. The SEARCH/LIST-gated fields describe the consuming surface, not this binding, and are answered none with a why. Ref S-083 (the next free ref: S-082 is binding_web_search, MF-44).

programme.why: Shared rendering infrastructure: the LIST binding the converted mobile LIST surfaces (first, the map page S-071) render through.
